items.text: Museums have their origins. <break time="0.8s" /> Both materially and conceptually. <break time="0.8s" /> In the collections of the wealthy and the privileged. <break time="0.8s" /> Historically, they displayed the wealth of the collector. <break time="0.8s" /> But also his cognitive power. <break time="0.8s" /> The acquisition and display of beautiful, curious, or rare objects. <break time="0.8s" /> In the Renaissance. <break time="0.8s" /> Confirmed the collectors access. <break time="0.8s" /> To the secrets of the universe contained in those objects. <break time="0.8s" /> Which mediated between the visible and the invisible. <break time="0.8s" /> The material world and the order that underlay it. <break time="0.8s" /> The collection indexed its proprietors access. <break time="0.8s" /> To this domain of hidden meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> And placed outsiders who were granted access to the collections. <break time="0.8s" /> In an inferior position. <break time="0.8s" /> Paying their respects to the collection. <break time="0.8s" /> They acknowledged the status of the collector. <break time="0.8s" /> Although the evolution of the collection into the museum. <break time="0.8s" /> During the early modern period. <break time="0.8s" /> Occurs along with a series of epistemic shifts. <break time="0.8s" /> In the structure of knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> Museums remain fundamentally concerned. <break time="0.8s" /> With expressing the relationship. <break time="0.8s" /> Of knowledge and ownership to identity, power, and status.
